title: A home you want. Money you have.
learn: A home has a price; savings are finite.
transition: The home enters first. The savings envelope opens beside it after a short hold. No debt terminology yet.
pacing: Home and envelope arrive separately; hold until Continue.
interaction: Continue, Back and Skip are always available. No financial interaction yet.
continuity: Home silhouette and original savings become the purchase context.
truth: Price £400,000.00; allocatable savings £100,000.00. Buying costs already set aside outside this illustration.

title: Some of your savings become your deposit.
learn: The deposit comes out of the same savings you already have.
transition: A broad coral ribbon leaves the savings envelope, travels left and becomes the house’s deposit band. The envelope visibly empties by the same amount.
pacing: Transit drawing: ribbon is a route, not additional money. Settle into 03; never hold duplicate monetary totals mid-transfer.
interaction: Demonstration first. Continue can settle immediately; no compulsory wait.
continuity: The ribbon resolves into the deposit boundary used by the calculator.
truth: Target deposit £40,000.00. No extra money is created during transfer.

title: You choose how much goes in.
learn: More deposit means less borrowing AND less money left outside.
transition: The ribbon settles. Borrowing fills the rest of the rectangular house body. A handle appears exactly on the shared deposit/borrowing boundary.
pacing: Hold indefinitely. After an optional adjustment, Continue follows this chosen deposit into the next experiment.
interaction: PROPOSED: drag the boundary; keyboard arrows or exact money entry give the same control. These are drawings, not working controls in R0.
continuity: One deposit state controls house fill and retained savings; Skip carries it forward.
truth: Deposit £40,000.00; mortgage £360,000.00; retained £60,000.00. Roof is decorative; the rectangular body alone encodes the purchase price.

title: Put more in. Borrow less.
learn: The extra deposit replaces borrowing pound for pound.
transition: Keep the house fixed. Lift its deposit boundary; let the old boundary remain as a dashed reference. The coral route visibly drains the envelope.
pacing: One proposed 700 ms transfer, then hold. Illustrative experiment: £40,000.00 to £80,000.00, not a new default.
interaction: PROPOSED: Try more makes an explicit comparison branch. Your original choice remains pinned; Back/Skip restores it.
continuity: Same house, envelope and deposit handle. Comparison is distinct from the user’s selected state.

title: Less debt to charge interest on.
learn: Borrowing less can reduce interest costs with the rate and repayment term held fixed.
transition: Follow a forest line from the mortgage region out of the house. It becomes an interest-cost trail outside the home. The previous larger trail stays as a dashed outline.
pacing: Reframe the debt edge; reveal the shorter trail only after the borrowing change settles. Hold before introducing pricing.
interaction: PROPOSED: replay this single cause and effect; no separate exercise.
continuity: Debt identity survives. The cost trail can later explain validated interest outputs.
truth: Conceptual comparison over the same repayment term. Trail lengths are schematic, not amounts. Interest is never part of the house price.

title: Sometimes you cross a pricing threshold.
learn: A better mortgage rate is conditional on reaching a deal band, not on every extra pound.
transition: The borrowing edge becomes a simple ruler. The marker reaches the fictional 80% borrowing boundary; only then does the attached rate tag turn over.
pacing: Two visible moments: marker reaches line, then tag changes. No smoothly decreasing rate animation.
interaction: PROPOSED: scrub across a supplied band boundary; retain a keyboard alternative. Real eligibility must come from validated data.
continuity: The same borrowing ratio later explains a calculator pricing step.
truth: Fictional 80% band example only; no lender offer or numeric rate. 80% means mortgage as a share of the home price. Actual bands may differ.

title: Now follow the monthly payment.
learn: Less borrowing, and possibly a lower rate, can reduce the required repayment for the same term.
transition: The mortgage region leads into a forest payment strip. Keep the original strip’s endpoint as an outline while the current payment retracts.
pacing: The house recedes; the payment strip becomes the focal object. Do not add saving labels until its contraction lands.
interaction: PROPOSED: optional replay; manual Continue. No auto-advance while someone is exploring.
continuity: Payment remains a separate monthly flow, never an opening asset.
truth: Conceptual monthly payment; no quoted repayment, no amount or scaled comparison. Same repayment term assumed.

title: The same monthly budget has room left.
learn: A lower payment leaves more of a fixed mortgage-and-saving budget available for saving.
transition: Reveal a fixed outer budget bracket around the payment strip from 07. Its freed space becomes a coral monthly-saving tab. That tab repeats once per month, not on purchase day.
pacing: Keep outer endpoints fixed. Shrink forest, expand coral; then one tab steps into the next month. Hold on the split.
interaction: PROPOSED: pause, replay or reverse. Saving/investing the surplus is an explicit comparison assumption.
continuity: The shared budget and contribution destination can later become inputs; no household affordability claim.
truth: Conceptual successor behaviour, unavailable from the current engine. No numeric budget, contribution or investment outcome is claimed.

title: Reverse it. Keep more at the start.
learn: The smaller deposit’s advantage is more money available immediately outside the home.
transition: Monthly tabs leave. Return to the exact house and envelope from 04. Reverse the coral transfer: deposit falls, borrowing expands, envelope refills.
pacing: Use the same route in reverse. Show the retained balance arriving before opening the next idea.
interaction: PROPOSED: Try less is a comparison experiment, not an overwrite of the user’s chosen deposit.
continuity: Original allocation and selected deposit remain recoverable throughout the story.
truth: Example B returns to £40,000.00 deposit; £360,000.00 mortgage; £60,000.00 retained.

title: Outside the home, you still have choices.
learn: Retained money is not automatically invested; cash and investments have different roles.
transition: The envelope opens into two clearly labelled sleeves. A cash reserve stays in the left sleeve; the optional allocation moves into the right sleeve only by choice.
pacing: Preserve the envelope outline while separating the destinations. Introduce uncertainty beside investments, not in fine print.
interaction: PROPOSED: choose Keep in cash or Invest some. R0 shows the investment branch only; neither is a recommendation.
continuity: Cash and investment destinations retain their meanings in the calculator.
truth: Illustrative B: £20,000.00 cash reserve plus £40,000.00 initially invested. Investments can lose value; cash is an alternative.

title: A head start, or more added each month?
learn: A smaller deposit can create a larger initial investment; a larger deposit may enable larger monthly additions.
transition: Open two labelled lanes sharing one start line. Initial balances are outlined containers. Later additions are small solid tabs at month markers. Show cash reserve separately in both lanes.
pacing: Reveal the opening containers first, then monthly tabs. Do not combine them into an unexplained growing total.
interaction: PROPOSED: inspect either lane. Neither is selected as a winner. Same monthly funding and surplus destination in both.
continuity: Opening allocation and monthly contribution remain separate fields and graphical objects.
truth: A: £80,000.00 deposit, £20,000.00 cash, £0.00 initial investment. B: £40,000.00 deposit, £20,000.00 cash, £40,000.00 initial investment. Monthly tab sizes are conceptual, not scaled financial outputs.

title: Then time changes the picture.
learn: Debt is repaid; cash and investments can change through contributions and returns.
transition: The monthly lane extends into a time rail. Keep three separate tracks: outstanding mortgage, cash and investments. Investment branches extend both upwards and downwards.
pacing: Advance one date marker across the same tracks; outline future states rather than invent balances. No crossover or maximum is drawn.
interaction: PROPOSED: pause the date marker or scrub it. Every view uses the same selected date.
continuity: The time rail becomes the comparison-date control. Opening deposit does not turn into growing equity.
truth: Conceptual, not to scale. No balances, probabilities, forecasts or ranked outcome. Future cash and debt depend on supported assumptions.

title: How much down — and when do you compare?
learn: Deposit and comparison date answer different questions.
transition: Bring the house and envelope back above the time rail. The teaching caption becomes a short question. The deposit handle and date marker gain visible input affordances in place.
pacing: Nothing resets. The same selected deposit and date persist; narration controls withdraw. In the illustrated branch, £40,000.00 and 10 years are retained.
interaction: PROPOSED: Finish or Skip from any beat lands here with the actual selected deposit, date and cash/investment choice.
continuity: House, retained money, deposit boundary and date rail become the familiar instrument.
truth: 10 years is an illustrative selected comparison horizon, not the mortgage term. R0 contains no calculated result.

title: The story becomes your instrument.
learn: The learner is already holding the controls needed to explore the decision.
transition: Keep 13’s house, envelope and rail in the same positions. Replace Continue with normal deposit/date inputs and a clear place for validated results to join this scene.
pacing: Mode change only: no redirect, no new dashboard, no reset. This is an endpoint sketch, not a settled calculator layout.
interaction: PROPOSED: change the same deposit/date; replay the guide without resetting either. Inputs pictured here are not live.
continuity: One illustration state and shared semantic components in guided and calculator modes. Advanced plots can join this vocabulary later.
truth: The full calculator, result composition, 2D/3D balance, advanced controls and access model remain undecided. No optimum has been calculated.
